sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises as the share of the credit limit in use goes up.
The number of past delinquencies is the second or third most important driver, and having at least one delinquency raises the predicted risk compared with having none.
Annual income is the second or third most important driver, and higher income lowers the predicted risk, with the largest drop above about $84,000.
Length of credit history has a weak to moderate effect, and longer histories lower the predicted risk.
The model shows no clear interaction between utilization and credit history length.
The data do not settle whether debt-to-income ratio has any effect on default risk at this sample size.
Recent credit inquiries hardly matter for the predicted risk.

The number of past delinquencies is the second or third most important driver, and the largest step in predicted risk comes between zero and one delinquency, with having at least one delinquency raising the predicted risk compared with having none.
Annual income is the second or third most important driver, and higher income generally lowers the predicted risk, with the largest drop above about $84,000.
Length of credit history has a weak to moderate effect, and longer histories lower the predicted risk.
The model shows no clear interaction between utilization and credit history length.
The data do not settle whether debt-to-income ratio has any effect on default risk at this sample size.
Income and age do not interact in the model, and recent credit inquiries hardly matter for the predicted risk.
